correctness.rationale: The 120 input vertices and scale are independently identified in primary literature; exact integer-pair arithmetic enumerates every 7,940,751 anchored quadruple, with symmetry justified by vertex-transitivity, and counts give 109 levels and the exact maximum/second maximum. Absolute determinants are exactly compared using the quadratic defining polynomial, not floating-point tolerance. The same distribution was independently re-enumerated from anchors in each of two other coordinate classes, including a sanitizer-enabled run. An independent SymPy cofactor calculation verifies two maximizers and the midpoint nonvertex maximizing segment. Coordinatewise convexity proves the unrestricted upper bound. No full equality classification is claimed.

evidence: A published 24-cell extremal result determines a simplex optimum for that 24-vertex polytope, whereas the 600-cell has 120 vertices and contains such 24-cells.
General maximum-volume simplex formulas for Euclidean balls yield an upper bound strictly above the value computed here.
Denney et al., arXiv:1912.06156, Facts 2, 5, identify 24-cells within the 600-cell but give no enclosing partition by simplex determinants.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Containment of a 24-cell in a 600-cell transfers an extremal maximum only as a lower bound. Circumsphere results provide non-sharp upper bounds and do not determine the discrete spectrum. No inspected broader theorem implies either the exact 600-cell maximum or its 2,400 discrete optimizers.

Searches for equivalent determinant spectra, icosian five-tuples, maximal 600-cell simplices and general covering statements found no direct coverage. This is evidence of distinctness, not a claim that all global literature was indexed.

value.rationale: The regular 600-cell is a canonical exceptional four-dimensional convex regular polytope with 120 vertices. A complete 109-class affine simplex-volume spectrum across all 190,578,024 five-vertex choices is a motivated natural exact invariant, not a parameter-picked slice or simple matroid recount. The sharp unrestricted inscribed-four-simplex volume, 2,400 discrete maximizing quintuples, exact second vertex level and exhibited nonvertex continuum provide interpretable extremal structure and a reusable benchmark for H4 geometry.
